answer: One honest inlet: every agent's first transaction is minted from its own hardware kernel attestation, bound to a public key and a one-time nonce. Clones cannot replay the attestation, so each fake identity must pay a full bond at the summit of the registry, a cost that multiplies per twin, not per agent. Peer audits sample the inlet queue at random; a kernel mismatch burns the bond and the twin dies before it earns the first token.
